quote: Under the new clause, Supplier can sell the business (or merge into another entity) and Harrowgate would be contractually bound to the successor with no right to approve, object, or terminate. ... Harrowgate could find itself exclusively sourcing from an unknown entity for years.
reason: The memo gets the mechanics right. It correctly identifies that Amendment No. 1 adds § 14.4, overriding § 14.3. That section lets Supplier assign without Customer's consent to Affiliates or to successors by merger or change of control. However, the criterion also requires two explanations the memo never gives. First, it never says that nothing prevents assignment to a Harrowgate competitor; it speaks only of an 'unknown entity' and financial strength. Second, it never says that Harrowgate remains bound by the § 14.3 consent requirement, so the restriction is now one-sided. Because these required elements are missing, the memo does not satisfy the issue in full.
